items.prompt:
A student wants to speak formally to his class. Which sentence should he say?
A) 'Uh, like, it rained a lot.'
B) 'It rained heavily last Tuesday afternoon.'

Identify which is formal and which is informal, and explain why.
items.answer: B is formal. B uses a complete sentence with specific, clear language ('rained heavily,' 'last Tuesday afternoon'). A is informal because it uses filler words ('Uh, like') and vague language ('a lot'). Formal speaking means using complete sentences and specific words.

steps: Formal: complete sentence, specific vocabulary, no filler words, appropriate for a class presentation.
Informal: filler words ('uh, like'), vague language ('a lot'), casual tone.
B is a complete sentence with specific details. A has filler words and no precision.
When presenting to a class or teacher, formal language is expected.

items.prompt:
A student says to the class: 'Um, yeah, the frog jumps.'
Rewrite this as a formal, complete sentence with more detail.
items.answer: Example rewrite: 'A frog uses its powerful back legs to jump long distances.' The rewrite removes informal filler words and adds specific detail to make the statement formal and informative.

steps: Remove filler words: 'Um, yeah,'.
Keep the core idea: a frog jumps.
Add specific detail to make it more formal and complete.
Rewrite example: 'A frog uses its powerful back legs to jump long distances.'

items.prompt:
'After eating breakfast every morning.'  
What is missing? Rewrite it as a complete sentence.
items.answer: Missing: both a subject and a main predicate. Example rewrite: 'After eating breakfast every morning, I brush my teeth.'

steps: This is only a dependent phrase — it sets up a time ('after eating breakfast') but does not complete a thought.
Add a subject and a main predicate to complete the sentence.
Rewrite example: 'After eating breakfast every morning, I brush my teeth.'

items.prompt:
Read these two sentences. Which is more appropriate for presenting to the class? Explain what makes it better.
A) 'Frogs are kinda cool and stuff.'
B) 'Frogs are interesting animals because they can live in water and on land.'
items.answer: B is more appropriate. It is a complete sentence with a clear subject, a predicate, and a reason introduced by 'because.' It uses specific, formal vocabulary. A uses informal filler phrases ('kinda,' 'and stuff') and does not give a reason or specific details.

steps: B has a complete sentence structure with a reason clause ('because...').
B uses formal vocabulary: 'interesting animals,' 'can live in water and on land.'
A uses informal language: 'kinda cool,' 'and stuff.'
For formal speaking, complete sentences with specific language are required.

items.prompt:
A student presents to the class and says: 'My favorite food. Pizza. It is good.'

Identify which part is a fragment and which is a complete sentence. Then rewrite the fragment as a complete sentence.
items.answer: 'My favorite food.' and 'Pizza.' are fragments — they have no predicates. 'It is good.' is a complete sentence. Rewrite: 'My favorite food is pizza.' or 'Pizza is my favorite food because it is cheesy and delicious.'

steps: 'My favorite food.' — subject only, no predicate. Fragment.
'Pizza.' — a noun alone, no predicate. Fragment.
'It is good.' — subject (It) + predicate (is good). Complete sentence.
Rewrite example: 'My favorite food is pizza because it is cheesy and delicious.'
